plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n of your value, which accounts for the number of competitors. With n=3, this means bidding 2/3 of my value. My value is $36, so optimal bid = 2/3 * 36 = $24. This balances winning probability against profit margin, maximizing expected profit given uncertainty about others' values.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., bid ≈ 2/3 of value. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $8, so I'll bid approximately $5.30 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against the other two bidders.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid for a first-price auction is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3) × value. My value is $44, so optimal bid ≈ $29.30. This balances winning probability against profit margin, avoiding overpaying while still competitive against others' similarly shaded bids.
